IMPACT OF THE PROPOSED ACTION
ON THE ENVIRONMENT
All domestic manufacturers of NPA's of 6,000 pounds and less GVWR, several Federal agencies including EPA and FEA, and several other interested parties commented on the draft EIS. Other comments applicable to the EIS were received in response to the NPRM. All comments have been summarized and analyzed in a previous section. The more substantive comments related to the effect of the MY 1979 emission standard for NPA's, the potential for reducing the weight of NPA's by MY 1979, the effect on NPA fuel economy of the MY 1979 emission standard for California, the increase in sulfate emissions in MY 1979 due to catalytic converter size increases, and the increased use of noble metals in catalysts for MY 1979. As a result of the analysis of all comments the agency is making several changes to the draft EIS. Gasoline savings are described in this final EIS relative to a range of fuel economies. The range was established by applying the maximum and minimum possible fuel economy penalties of the MY 1979 emission standard to the originally proposed AFES. Also, gasoline savings are shown for two classes of NPA's. The two classes are 1) recreational type NPA's with off-road capability and 2) all other NPA's.
